post/coa-forced-status.json.why: #38 evidence for the derived target lifecycle_status_history (Spec 124 R-ET, first live use, Night P4 2026-10-20; R-GZ fit-to-width): the first 50 coa_applications rows of the live Active feed (last_seen_at = the last run's clock) get ' forced' fitted into data_hash (varchar(64), the guard column) and appended to status (varchar(50), the R-DY derive.prior_columns column) in one transaction; the converted step's prior-status read sees a changed status, deriveRows writes exactly one ledger row per cohort key (lifecycle_status_history_written 50, R-DN count_path) and the guarded upsert heals both columns (records_updated 50). Restore deletes the 50 gained ledger rows by natural key and verifies the primary pair. The derived rows carry the run clock, so the lifecycle_status_history hash of this capture churns on every --replay-all; that churn is expected, not drift.

post/coa-forced-data-hash.json.why: #38 evidence for coa_applications (Spec 124 R-CZ append_text with R-GZ fit-to-width, Night P4 2026-10-20): the first 50 Active-feed rows get ' forced' fitted into data_hash (sha256 hex, always 64 chars in varchar(64)); the guarded upsert (guard data_hash, is_distinct_from) rewrites and heals all 50 (records_updated 50, lifecycle_status_history_written 0: status untouched, so no ledger row). coa writes two tables, so this capture is named per table in cohort.json.
